name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOTION_IN_A_PLANE_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Classification and definitions of fundamental kinematic quantities

questiontext.text:
Match the items in List I with the corresponding descriptions or expressions in List II:

List I (Physical Quantity)List II (Definition and Dimension)
(A) Distance(I) Rate of change of velocity with dimensions \([\text{M}^0\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}]\)
(B) Velocity(II) Total path length traversed with SI unit metre
(C) Acceleration(III) Quantity of matter with dimensions \([\text{M}\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]\)
(D) Mass(IV) Rate of change of displacement with dimensions \([\text{M}^0\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Matching for item (A) Distance
Distance is the scalar measure of the actual total path length traversed by an object during its motion between two points, having the SI unit of metre (\(\text{m}\)). Therefore, item (A) matches with entry II.

Step 2: Matching for item (B) Velocity
Velocity is defined as the time rate of change of displacement, which is a vector quantity having the dimensions of \([\text{M}^0\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]\). Therefore, item (B) matches with entry IV.

Step 3: Matching for item (C) Acceleration
Acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity, which is a vector quantity with dimensions of \([\text{M}^0\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}]\). Therefore, item (C) matches with entry I.

Step 4: Matching for item (D) Mass
Mass is an intrinsic scalar property representing the quantity of matter within a body, having the base physical dimension of \([\text{M}\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]\). Therefore, item (D) matches with entry III.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated pairings gives the complete correct match: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOTION_IN_A_PLANE_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Mathematical expressions governing parameters in projectile motion

questiontext.text:
Match the items in List I with the corresponding descriptions or expressions in List II:

List I (Projectile Parameter)List II (Mathematical Formula)
(A) Time of flight(I) \(\frac{v_0^2}{g}\)
(B) Maximum height(II) \(\frac{2v_0 \sin\theta_0}{g}\)
(C) Horizontal range(III) \(\frac{v_0^2 \sin^2\theta_0}{2g}\)
(D) Maximum horizontal range(IV) \(\frac{v_0^2 \sin(2\theta_0)}{g}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Matching for item (A) Time of flight
The total time during which a projectile remains in the air between launch and landing on level ground is derived by setting vertical displacement \(y = 0\): \(v_0 \sin\theta_0 t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 0\), which yields \(T_f = \frac{2v_0 \sin\theta_0}{g}\). Therefore, item (A) matches with entry II.

Step 2: Matching for item (B) Maximum height
At the apex of the trajectory, the vertical velocity component is zero (\(v_y = 0\)). Using \(v_y^2 = v_{0y}^2 - 2gh_m\) gives \(0 = (v_0 \sin\theta_0)^2 - 2gh_m\), hence \(h_m = \frac{v_0^2 \sin^2\theta_0}{2g}\). Therefore, item (B) matches with entry III.

Step 3: Matching for item (C) Horizontal range
The horizontal distance traveled during the time of flight is \(R = v_{0x} T_f = (v_0 \cos\theta_0)\left(\frac{2v_0 \sin\theta_0}{g}\right) = \frac{v_0^2 \sin(2\theta_0)}{g}\). Therefore, item (C) matches with entry IV.

Step 4: Matching for item (D) Maximum horizontal range
The range achieves its maximum value when the trigonometric factor \(\sin(2\theta_0) = 1\) (at \(\theta_0 = 45^\circ\)), giving \(R_{\max} = \frac{v_0^2}{g}\). Therefore, item (D) matches with entry I.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated pairings gives the complete correct match: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOTION_IN_A_PLANE_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Formulae relating parameters in uniform circular motion

questiontext.text:
Match the items in List I with the corresponding descriptions or expressions in List II:

List I (Circular Motion Variable)List II (Equivalent Relation)
(A) Angular speed in terms of linear speed(I) \(4\pi^2 \nu^2 R\)
(B) Centripetal acceleration in terms of angular speed(II) \(\frac{2\pi R}{T}\)
(C) Centripetal acceleration in terms of frequency(III) \(\frac{v}{R}\)
(D) Linear speed in terms of time period(IV) \(\omega^2 R\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Matching for item (A) Angular speed in terms of linear speed
The linear speed along the circular path of radius \(R\) relates to the angular speed \(\omega\) by \(v = \omega R\). Solving for angular speed gives \(\omega = \frac{v}{R}\). Therefore, item (A) matches with entry III.

Step 2: Matching for item (B) Centripetal acceleration in terms of angular speed
The centripetal acceleration magnitude is \(a_c = \frac{v^2}{R}\). Substituting \(v = \omega R\) yields \(a_c = \frac{(\omega R)^2}{R} = \omega^2 R\). Therefore, item (B) matches with entry IV.

Step 3: Matching for item (C) Centripetal acceleration in terms of frequency
The angular speed is related to frequency of revolution \(\nu\) by \(\omega = 2\pi \nu\). Substituting into the centripetal acceleration formula gives \(a_c = \omega^2 R = (2\pi \nu)^2 R = 4\pi^2 \nu^2 R\). Therefore, item (C) matches with entry I.

Step 4: Matching for item (D) Linear speed in terms of time period
In one complete period \(T\), the particle travels a distance equal to the circumference \(2\pi R\). Hence, the speed is \(v = \frac{2\pi R}{T}\). Therefore, item (D) matches with entry II.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated pairings gives the complete correct match: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOTION_IN_A_PLANE_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Resultant magnitude of equal vectors at various angles

questiontext.text:
Match the items in List I with the corresponding descriptions or expressions in List II:

List I (Angle between equal vectors of magnitude P)List II (Resultant Vector Magnitude)
(A) \(\theta = 0^\circ\)(I) \(\sqrt{3}\,P\)
(B) \(\theta = 60^\circ\)(II) \(\sqrt{2}\,P\)
(C) \(\theta = 90^\circ\)(III) \(P\)
(D) \(\theta = 120^\circ\)(IV) \(2P\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Formula for Resultant of Two Equal Vectors
For two vectors of equal magnitude \(P\) inclined at an angle \(\theta\), the law of cosines gives the resultant magnitude: \(R = \sqrt{P^2 + P^2 + 2P^2\cos\theta} = \sqrt{2P^2(1 + \cos\theta)} = \sqrt{4P^2 \cos^2(\theta/2)} = 2P\cos(\theta/2)\).

Step 2: Matching for item (A) at angle 0 degrees
When \(\theta = 0^\circ\), \(\cos(0^\circ/2) = \cos(0^\circ) = 1\), which yields \(R = 2P(1) = 2P\). Therefore, item (A) matches with entry IV.

Step 3: Matching for item (B) at angle 60 degrees
When \(\theta = 60^\circ\), \(\cos(60^\circ/2) = \cos(30^\circ) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), which yields \(R = 2P\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{3}\,P\). Therefore, item (B) matches with entry I.

Step 4: Matching for item (C) at angle 90 degrees
When \(\theta = 90^\circ\), \(\cos(90^\circ/2) = \cos(45^\circ) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), which yields \(R = 2P\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \sqrt{2}\,P\). Therefore, item (C) matches with entry II.

Step 5: Matching for item (D) at angle 120 degrees
When \(\theta = 120^\circ\), \(\cos(120^\circ/2) = \cos(60^\circ) = \frac{1}{2}\), which yields \(R = 2P\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = P\). Therefore, item (D) matches with entry III.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated pairings gives the complete correct match: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.
